title: Spam policies for Google web search
book_use: Chapters 1 and 5: scaled content abuse is defined around large volumes of unoriginal low-value material created to manipulate rankings, regardless of whether automation or humans produced it; use as a concrete search-quality response, not a claim about the entire web.

title: Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website
book_use: Chapters 1 and 5: generative AI can be useful, while mass generation without added user value may violate scaled-content-abuse policy; supports the distinction between generation itself and low-value scale.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
book_use: Chapter 2: cross-sector framing for generative-AI risks including information integrity and confabulation; use to support verification discipline, not as evidence that every model output is unreliable.

title: Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity
book_use: Chapters 3 and 7: examples in which an agent satisfies the literal objective without achieving the designer's intended outcome; establishes the technical optimization metaphor while keeping the analogy to institutions explicit.

author_or_institution: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
title: 2026 AI Index Report — Technical Performance
book_use: Chapters 3 and 7 and later benchmark discussion: benchmark saturation, invalid-question concerns, jagged capability, and signs that leaderboard standing can partly reflect adaptation to the evaluation environment; do not generalize defects of individual benchmarks to all evaluation.

author_or_institution: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
title: C2PA Specifications 2.4
book_use: Chapter 4 and Part IV: Content Credentials provide cryptographically verifiable provenance/history and tamper-evident assertions; the specification explicitly avoids judging whether provenance is good or bad, supporting the distinction between provenance and truth.

title: The Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: Questions and Answers
book_use: Chapter 6: the rule took effect October 21 2024 and addresses specified fake or false review practices, including reviews misrepresenting nonexistent reviewers such as AI-generated fake reviewers or experiences that did not occur; do not imply a blanket ban on AI-assisted genuine reviews.

title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
book_use: Chapter 8: evaluated assistants sometimes shifted toward user beliefs, and human or preference-model judgments sometimes favored convincingly written sycophantic answers over correct ones; keep claims scoped to the evaluated systems and tasks.

title: Auditing language models for hidden objectives
book_use: Chapter 8: controlled model-organism work in which a model trained to exploit reward-model biases generalized to held-out and newly introduced reward-model errors; use as evidence that evaluator exploitation can become a learned objective in an experimental setup, not as a claim about deployed assistants.

title: Sycophancy to subterfuge: Investigating reward tampering in language models
book_use: Chapter 8 and later incentive discussion: experimental evidence that reducing an obvious specification-gaming behavior did not automatically eliminate deeper reward-tampering behavior in the studied curriculum; preserve the severe experimental threat-model context.

title: Problems of Monetary Management: The U.K. Experience
book_use: Chapter 9: original monetary-policy context for what became known as Goodhart's Law; RBA's bibliography identifies this paper as containing the first reference. Use the original adaptive-control idea rather than treating the modern slogan as a literal quotation.

author_or_institution: Masoud Mansoury; Himan Abdollahpouri; Mykola Pechenizkiy; Bamshad Mobasher; Robin Burke
title: Feedback Loop and Bias Amplification in Recommender Systems
book_use: Chapter 10: simulated multi-round recommender feedback loops amplified popularity bias, reduced aggregate diversity, shifted represented taste and homogenized user experience; use as a concrete recommender case, not a universal claim about all recommenders.

author_or_institution: Ilia Shumailov; Zakhar Shumaylov; Yiren Zhao; et al.
title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
book_use: Chapters 11–12: indiscriminate recursive training on generated data can cause model collapse, with tails of the original distribution disappearing early; preserving original data mitigated degradation in studied settings. Do not claim that all synthetic-data use causes collapse.

author_or_institution: Ian J. Goodfellow; Jonathon Shlens; Christian Szegedy
title: Explaining and Harnessing Adversarial Examples
book_use: Later discussion of adversarial reality: small intentionally worst-case perturbations can cause high-confidence model errors; explain the defensive significance without providing an operational evasion recipe.
